sourceFindings: Provisioning grants SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on all four measurement tables; its verification requires the same broad privileges. Both grant and verification must change together.

Existing consent revoke locks the contributor, inserts/updates its revocation, then directly deletes receipts in the same transaction. Existing whole-account erase locks operation and sorted contributors, fences contributors, deletes receipts and updates the durable operation.

The installed-source account guard is a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE receipt trigger. Fixed routines must preserve actual schema, current intake/fence checks, contributor locks, immutable account-operation manifest, and both foreign-key cascades.
Restrict receipt UPDATE to the actual receipt field needed by the existing writer; a generic UPDATE grant is not the chosen bounded policy. Do not derive the field from simplified fixtures.
No actual production ACL/schema inspection or migration was performed for this review.
coordinatedChange: Adapt and test both existing revoke and whole-account erase against bounded owner functions before removing runtime direct DELETE; update provisioning grants and its verification in the same source change.
Do not import the fixture contributor-revocation seam. It lacks actual guard/admission/locks and stores a contributor-linked origin journal with unaccepted unlink/retention behavior.
A missing role/function, service permission failure or store outage must remain 503/unavailable/pending, never DRIVER_CONSENT_REVOKED.

Account erasure keeps the original operation UUID and accepted immutable manifest. Internal store retries with uncertain outcome must resolve only that original origin; the legacy HTTP repeated DELETE is not proof of origin-probe-only enforcement.
Keep production migration, grants, native delivery, activation and restore acceptance as separate unperformed gates.
